subject: physics
title: Thermal Physics Adventure 2: Specific latent heat and phase change
welcome_lead: Today you'll melt ice and boil water — measuring latent heat.
meta_desc: Physics — phase change, latent heat of fusion + vaporisation, plateau, kinetic theory.
final_note: You learned q = mL for phase changes; T stays constant during change as energy breaks bonds; L_v ≫ L_f for water.

concepts.def: Energy per kg to change phase

walkthroughs.body_html:
On a heating curve, T rises until phase change, then is constant during change.

Energy goes into breaking intermolecular bonds, not raising T.

For water: L_f = 334 kJ/kg (melt), L_v = 2260 kJ/kg (boil).
Boiling needs ~6.8× more — explains why boiling burns are worse than melting ones.

q = mL for phase change.
q = mcΔT for temperature change.

Heat 0.5 kg ice at -10°C to steam at 100°C:
1. Warm ice: 0.5 × 2100 × 10 = 10,500 J.
2. Melt ice: 0.5 × 334000 = 167,000 J.
3. Warm water: 0.5 × 4180 × 100 = 209,000 J.
4. Boil water: 0.5 × 2,260,000 = 1,130,000 J.
Total ~1.5 MJ.

During heating phase change:
- KE constant (so T constant).
- PE rises (bonds breaking).

Conversely on cooling.

Sweating cools you because evaporation removes latent heat from your skin (~2.4 kJ per g of sweat).
